overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of how the ontology of flesh reframes subject, world, and nature. You'll be asked about the Nature lectures, Uexküll's Umwelt, the flesh of the world, and the major critiques of the flesh ontology.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Which two views of nature does Merleau-Ponty reject in his lectures?

options.html: Nature as pure object and nature as product of mind
options.text: Nature as pure object and nature as product of mind
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Both set nature over against a subject. For Merleau-Ponty, nature has its own meaning.

options.html: Nature as living and nature as meaningful
options.text: Nature as living and nature as meaningful
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. He holds that nature is living and meaningful. He rejects nature as pure object and as product of mind.

options.html: Nature as studied by biology and nature as painted
options.text: Nature as studied by biology and nature as painted
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. He draws on biology. He rejects nature as pure object and as product of mind.

options.html: Nature as process and nature as productive
options.text: Nature as process and nature as productive
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. He finds resources in these views. He rejects nature as pure object and as product of mind.

forms.stemHtml: Why do a tick and a bird in the same forest live in different worlds, on Uexküll's account?

options.html: Because they occupy different physical locations
options.text: Because they occupy different physical locations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Even in the same place, their meaningful surroundings differ.

options.html: Because different features matter to each through its actions
options.text: Because different features matter to each through its actions
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each animal's Umwelt is defined by what it perceives and does.

options.html: Because each forms a private mental image of the forest
options.text: Because each forms a private mental image of the forest
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The Umwelt is defined by perception and action, not by mental images.

options.html: Because the forest changes depending on the time of day
options.text: Because the forest changes depending on the time of day
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The difference lies in what matters to each animal.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following accurately state a critique of the flesh ontology? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Irigaray: reversibility can't register sexual difference
options.text: Irigaray: reversibility can't register sexual difference
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! She reads it as a closed circuit of a body relating to itself.

options.html: Levinas: modeling others on reversibility reduces their alterity
options.text: Levinas: modeling others on reversibility reduces their alterity
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! For Levinas, the ethical relation is asymmetrical.

options.html: Some critics: "flesh" is too vague to do theoretical work
options.text: Some critics: "flesh" is too vague to do theoretical work
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The term is used for body, world, language, and ideas.

options.html: Irigaray: the ontology gives too much weight to touch
options.text: Irigaray: the ontology gives too much weight to touch
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Irigaray argues that it privileges vision and forgets an earlier tactile life.
Sorry, that's incorrect. Levinas objects that reversibility is symmetrical, while the ethical relation is not.

forms.stemHtml: What is Uexküll's German term for an animal's meaningful surroundings, made up of the features that matter to it through its perception and action? Enter one word.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Different animals in the same place live in different Umwelten.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Uexküll's term is Umwelt.

forms.stemHtml: On the flesh ontology, how are subject and world related?

options.html: As two substances linked by causal interaction
options.text: As two substances linked by causal interaction
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. They aren't two things to connect. They're differentiations of one fabric.

options.html: As a mind and the world it constructs
options.text: As a mind and the world it constructs
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The world isn't a product of mind. Subject and world are differentiations of one fabric.
Correct! Like two surfaces of one folded cloth.

options.html: As identical, with no distinction at all
options.text: As identical, with no distinction at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. They're distinct, though made of one fabric.

title: Subject, World, and Nature
